name: Bloomberg
tagline: Subscription financial news, market data and analysis from the company that also rents out the Terminal.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: You are not paying for a website, you are paying for a newsroom of roughly two thousand journalists and a data operation that has been buying, cleaning and normalizing market data since the 1980s. An agent can absolutely build you a slick markets dashboard with a watchlist, charts and a news river in an afternoon. What it cannot build is the story nobody else has yet, or a clean corporate ownership graph, or intraday depth that is right often enough to trade on. The consolation build is genuinely useful as an information cockpit and genuinely useless as a substitute for reporting. Also note the Terminal, the real business here, costs more per year than most people's cars and is not on the table at all.
coreLoopDIY: A local dashboard that pulls free RSS feeds and public market quotes into one watchlist-driven news-and-price cockpit with keyword alerts.
requirements: free market data source such as Stooq or a keyed Alpha Vantage / Finnhub tier
public RSS feeds you are allowed to read
optional OpenAI-compatible key if you want summaries
whatYouLose: Original reporting and scoops, which is the entire product
Cleaned, survivorship-adjusted historical and fundamental data
Reliable intraday and depth-of-book pricing; free feeds are delayed and flaky
Anything Terminal-side: chat, IB, screening, the analytics library
moatNotes: The data moat and the newsroom moat reinforce each other, and the Terminal's messaging network makes the whole thing sticky for the people who actually pay full price.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because in finance being wrong is expensive and being late is worse. People pay for a source they can cite in a meeting without hedging, for numbers that reconcile with what everyone else on the call is looking at, and for the small number of stories a year that move a position. A hobby dashboard gives you headlines you already could have found and prices you would not size a trade on. That gap is not a coding problem.
notes: The dashboard is a weekend, the reporting is not. The moat is a global newsroom plus four decades of cleaned market data that everyone in the room already agrees to treat as ground truth.
prompt:
Build a local financial news and markets dashboard called "deskterminal". Single user, runs on my laptop, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud.

Stack, no substitutions: Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLite via plain sqlite3, Jinja2 templates, htmx for partial refreshes, and vanilla CSS in one file. Charts with uPlot from a CDN. APScheduler for background polling. No React, no Docker, no ORM.

Features in scope:
1. Watchlist: I add tickers in the UI, stored in SQLite. Each row shows last price, day change, and a 90 day sparkline.
2. Price fetching: pull daily and, if available, delayed intraday quotes from a provider configured in .env (support Stooq CSV with no key as the default, and optionally Finnhub or Alpha Vantage if API_KEY is set). Cache every response in SQLite so restarts are cheap and rate limits are respected.
3. News river: poll a list of RSS/Atom feeds from feeds.txt with feedparser. Deduplicate by URL and by normalized title. Store publisher, title, link, published_at, and raw summary.
4. Ticker tagging: naive but useful. Match company names and tickers from my watchlist against headlines and store the matches, so clicking a ticker filters the river to stories that mention it.
5. Alerts: keyword rules and percent-move rules stored in SQLite. When one fires, write a row to an alerts table and show a badge in the header. Desktop notification via a shell hook if NOTIFY_CMD is set in .env.
6. Optional summaries: if OPENAI_API_KEY is set, add a button that summarizes the last 24 hours of tagged headlines for one ticker into five bullets. If the key is absent, hide the button entirely, do not stub it.

Explicitly out of scope: authentication, multi-user, real-time websockets, order entry, portfolio accounting, backtesting, mobile app, scraping paywalled articles. Store only links and the summary text the feed itself publishes.

Deliverables: app.py, db.py, feeds.txt, requirements.txt, .env.example, templates/, static/, and a README with a one-command start. Seed feeds.txt with a handful of freely available public business feeds and a comment telling me to check each publisher's terms. Include a make-style script that runs the poller once so I can see data on first launch.
